title: Pro-etale composition on a compatible tower has the open-adjoint normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:U\to V$ and $f:V\to W$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Supply compactifications [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]
$$V\xrightarrow{i}\overline V\xrightarrow{q}W,\qquad U\xrightarrow{a}\overline U\xrightarrow{p}\overline V,\qquad pa=ih.$$
Put $H=\overline U\times_{\overline V}V$, with projections $b:H\hookrightarrow\overline U$, $r:H\to V$, and induced open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow H$, so $bj=a$, $rj=h$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle]. Use ordinary constant-$\Lambda$ pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with $P_t=Rt_{p,*}$ and $J_v=v_{p,!}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $\operatorname{Ex}^p:i_p^*P_p\to P_rb_p^*$ be the unit--square--counit exchange of this Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. On $N$ of bounded-below etale origin [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], put
$$\lambda_N=P_r(\eta_{b,N}^{-1})\circ\operatorname{Ex}^p_{J_bN}:i_p^*P_pJ_bN\xrightarrow{\sim}P_rN,$$
where $\eta_b:1\xrightarrow{\sim}b_p^*J_b$ is the open-adjunction unit [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Let $\gamma_N:J_iP_rN\to P_pJ_bN$ be the adjoint of $\lambda_N^{-1}$ under $J_i\dashv i_p^*$; equivalently $\lambda_N\circ i_p^*(\gamma_N)\circ\eta_{i,P_rN}=1$.
For $L\in D^+(U_e,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $M=\nu_U^*L$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the canonical composition map $\alpha^p_{f,h,M}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition] on the candidates $(j,r),(i,q),(a,qp)$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is exactly
$$P_qJ_iP_rJ_jM\xrightarrow{P_q\gamma_{J_jM}}P_qP_pJ_bJ_jM\xrightarrow{D_{q,p}\,E_{b,j}}P_{qp}J_aM.$$
Here $D_{q,p}:P_qP_p\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{qp}$ is the inverse of the canonical derived-direct-image comparison [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], and $E_{b,j}:J_bJ_j\xrightarrow{\sim}J_a$ is the adjunction compositor conjugate to composite open restriction [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. In particular this is an equality for the specified composition map, and $\gamma$ is invertible on these witnessed inputs. No properness of either $h$ or $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Construction, displayed proper/open map and following composition paragraph; Stacks Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, compatible-tower model. The identification with the open-adjoint normalization is an agent assertion.

proof.text: Apply the compatible-triangle statement with $X=U$, $Y=V$, $Z=W$, $f=h$, $g=f$, $c=j$ and $p_Y=r$. It gives $bj=a$, $rj=h$, that $b$ is open and $r$ is proper, and that $pb=ir$ is Cartesian; the three candidates in the item are therefore compactifications. The coefficient ring $\Lambda$ is finite by its coefficient-datum definition. All schemes needed below are Noetherian: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$; apply finite-type-over-Noetherian first to the supplied finite-type $k$-schemes and then to the proper arrows $q,p$ (proper includes finite type), and use the open-subscheme lemma for $H$. They are quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian lemma. Thus the permanence lemma makes $p,r$ qcqs. This verifies the hypotheses of the general Noetherian-scheme site tools used below, over the original arbitrary field $k$.

source.place: Construction, compatible compactifications and Cartesian square

proof.text: Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$. Exactness of $C$, of etale open extension, and of pro-etale open extension lets the sheaf comparison $C_Hj_!^e\simeq J_jC_U$ descend termwise to bounded-below complexes. Consequently $N=J_jM$ has the explicit witness $K=j_!^eL\in D^+(H_e,\Lambda)$ and $C_HK\simeq N$. The same argument for $b$ gives the witness $b_!^eK$ for $J_bN$. More generally, whenever $N=C_HK$ is supplied with a bounded-below etale witness, the latter construction supplies the required witness for $J_bN$. These are exactly the triples in the etale-origin category definition.

source.place: Construction, etale-origin N and extension by zero of a complex on U

proof.text:
For the square $H\xrightarrow{b}\overline U$, $V\xrightarrow{i}\overline V$, with vertical arrows $r,p$, use the site clause of the proper/open coefficient-mate lemma with $A=B=R=\Lambda$. Its hypotheses are exactly Step 1, and its input is the witness $K$ of Step 2. Denote its specified pro-etale arrow by $T_N:J_iP_rN\to P_pJ_bN$. If $e_v:CJ_v^e\simeq J_vC$ and $d_t:CRt_*^e\simeq P_tC$ are the named site comparisons, that lemma gives the actual formula
$$T_{C_HK}=P_p(e_{b,K})\,d_{p,b_!^eK}\,C_{\overline V}(\Gamma_Q^e(K))\,(J_i(d_{r,K})\,e_{i,Rr_*^eK})^{-1}.$$
Here $\Gamma_Q^e$ is the specified etale proper/open map. Its representative is $i_!^er_*^eI\cong p_*^eb_!^eI\to p_*^eI'$ for a K-injective $I$ representing $K$ and a resolution $b_!^eI\to I'$. The interchange-coherence statement supplies precisely this representative for its map $\gamma_Q$; the map named in the coefficient-mate statement is $\Gamma_Q$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], whose statement specifies the same representative $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I$ on a K-injective $J$, and a K-injective representative of a bounded-below complex is one in the unbounded category. Hence $\gamma_Q=\Gamma_Q^{\rm et}$ on $D^+$, which is the map the composition construction transports. Thus $T$ is the named site transport of this canonical arrow, with no choice of automorphism.

source.place: Construction, specified proper/open map; Stacks Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open

proof.text:
The site clause in Step 3 prescribes $T$ as the open adjunct of the inverse of the transported open-restriction exchange followed by the inverse open unit. Identify those transported maps explicitly. Apply the exchange-transport statement with $(f,f',g,g')=(p,r,i,b)$ and the etale complex $b_!^eK$; $p,r$ are qcqs by Step 1. Its equation $T_L C(E_L)=\operatorname{Ex}^R_{\square,C L} S_L$ identifies the transported exchange with exactly the ambient ringed exchange in the item, for the constant ring $\Lambda$. The open-comparison unit-normalization equation for $b$ identifies the transported etale unit with $\eta_b$. All these equations descend termwise by the exactness in Step 2. Hence the transported open-restriction map is precisely
$$\lambda_N=P_r(\eta_{b,N}^{-1})\operatorname{Ex}^p_{J_bN}.$$
It is invertible: proper base change applies to $J_bN$ with the witness from Step 2, and the open unit is invertible by the derived open-adjunction statement.

source.place: Construction, proper base change over V; identification of the named exchange and open unit

proof.text: The open-adjunction prescription in the site clause now says $T_N=\varepsilon_{i,P_pJ_bN}\circ J_i(\lambda_N^{-1})$. Its transpose is therefore $i_p^*(T_N)\circ\eta_{i,P_rN}=\lambda_N^{-1}$. The item defines $\gamma_N$ by the same transpose. Injectivity of the Hom bijection for $J_i\dashv i_p^*$ gives $T_N=\gamma_N$, naturally in each witnessed $N$. This step proves equality of the specified maps; it makes no inference about invertibility of their adjuncts.

source.place: Construction, open-adjunction prescription and uniqueness of its transpose

proof.text:
Fix the final compositors. The finite-level direct-image statement gives $D_{q,p}=c_{q,p}^{-1}:P_qP_p\simeq P_{qp}$, with the identity normalization asserted there. For open extension, the two open Hom bijections give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(J_bJ_jM,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j_p^*b_p^*F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,a_p^*F).$$
The middle comparison is the canonical composite restriction, since $bj=a$. Apply the conjugate-isomorphism unit-equation statement to these two left adjoints of canonically identified restrictions. It gives the unique unit-preserving isomorphism $E_{b,j}:J_bJ_j\simeq J_a$, whose conjugate is that restriction comparison. For an identity open it is the identity by the same uniqueness. This fixes the exact $E$ required in the item, rather than an arbitrary natural isomorphism of these functors.

source.place: Construction, final composition of proper direct images and of open extensions

proof.text:
Compute the composition by carrying out its Construction paragraph on the supplied models. The candidate definition identifies its source as $P_qJ_iP_rJ_jM$ and its target as $P_{qp}J_aM$. The construction first applies its displayed proper/open arrow $A_N:J_iP_rN\to P_pJ_bN$ to $N=J_jM$. It specifies this arrow over $V$ by proper base change: with the open units inserted, its restriction is the inverse of $i_p^*P_pJ_bN\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}^p}P_rb_p^*J_bN\xrightarrow{P_r(\eta_b^{-1})}P_rN$. Thus $i_p^*(A_N)\eta_{i,P_rN}=\lambda_N^{-1}$, using the precise exchange and unit identified in Step 4. The open Hom bijection gives $A_N=T_N$ by Step 5. The etale representative of this map is the one in Step 3, and the coefficient-mate site's equation fixes its transport as an equality of maps. Now apply $P_q$ and then the compositors fixed in Step 6. The sequence prescribed by the construction is exactly
$$P_qJ_iP_rJ_jM\xrightarrow{P_qT_{J_jM}}P_qP_pJ_bJ_jM\xrightarrow{D_{q,p}\,E_{b,j}}P_{qp}J_aM.$$
Replacing $T$ by $\gamma$ proves the formula. Here the composition theorem supplies preservation of witnessed inputs and its canonical composition isomorphisms; the two-arrow formula is proved by this expansion of the construction, not read into that theorem's statement.

source.place: Construction, apply proper/open interchange to extension by zero and push by Rq; Stacks Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, four-line computation

proof.text:
For invertibility, perform the same construction on the pair $r:H\to V$, $i:V\to\overline V$. Compactify $i$ by $(i,\mathrm{id})$ and $ir$ by $(b,p)$; the fibre-product open is $H$, its projection is $r$, and its source open is $\mathrm{id}_H$. The computation in Step 7 gives $\alpha^p_{i,r}=T$ under the identity-open proper models. The remaining identity direct-image compositor is the identity by the direct-image composition statement, and the identity open compositor is the identity by Step 6. For the pair $b,p$ choose instead $(\mathrm{id}_{\overline U},p)$ and $(b,\mathrm{id}_{\overline U})$. The square has identity vertical arrows; its exchange and open adjunct are identities by the unit--square--counit formula and open triangle identities. Equivalently its identity-square open comparison is the identity as specified by the open-square-exchange statement. Thus $\alpha^p_{p,b}$ is the identity on the candidate $P_pJ_b$. Consequently the square comparison
$$\chi=(\alpha^p_{p,b})^{-1}\circ\alpha^p_{i,r}:J_iP_r\longrightarrow P_pJ_b$$
(using $(\mathrm{id},r)$ and $(\mathrm{id},p)$ for proper coincidence) is $T=\gamma$. Both $\alpha$ factors are isomorphisms on witnessed inputs by the composition theorem, so $\gamma$ is invertible there. This proves the last clause from composition isomorphisms, independently of any claim that taking an adjunct preserves invertibility.
